cases.sentence: ___ до последней кадрили был для Кити волшебным сновидением радостных цветов, звуков и движений.
cases.translation: The whole ball, until the last quadrille, was for Kitty a magical dream of joyful colors, sounds, and movements.
cases.explain: Бал is the subject of был (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Она не танцевала только, когда чувствовала себя слишком усталую и просила ___.
cases.translation: She danced except when she felt too tired and asked for rest.
cases.explain: The verb просить (to ask for) governs the genitive case for the thing requested.

cases.sentence: Ей случилось быть виз-а-ви с Вронским и Анной, к ее ___ она заметила перемену в его лице.
cases.translation: It happened that she was vis-à-vis Vronsky and Anna; to her good fortune, she noticed the change in his face.
cases.explain: The preposition к (to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Лицо Китти только выражением отчаяния и удивления ответило на ее ___.
cases.translation: Kitty's face answered her smile only with an expression of despair and surprise.
cases.explain: The preposition на (to, toward) with the verb ответить governs the accusative case.

cases.translation: She waited for the 'Mazurka' with her heart sinking.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Когда Вронский увидал ее, столкнувшись с нею в ___.
cases.translation: When Vronsky saw her, having run into her during the mazurka.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in, during) indicating a point in the dance governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Вронский с Китти прошел несколько туров вальса.
reading.question: What did Vronsky and Kitty do together after the previous chapter's events?
options: They danced several turns of the waltz
reading.correct: They danced several turns of the waltz
reading.explain: The text states Vronsky went through several turns of the waltz with Kitty.

reading.ru: Но Китти и не ожидала большего от кадрильи.
reading.question: What was Kitty's attitude toward the quadrille with Vronsky, since little of note was said?
options: She hadn't expected much more from the quadrille anyway
She was devastated by the lack of conversation
She demanded he say something meaningful
She refused to finish the dance
reading.correct: She hadn't expected much more from the quadrille anyway
reading.explain: The text notes that Kitty had not expected anything more from the quadrille, since nothing significant was said during it.

reading.ru: Она не танцевала только, когда чувствовала себя слишком усталую и просила отдыха.
reading.question: Under what circumstance did Kitty avoid dancing that evening?
options: Only when she felt too tired and asked for rest
Only when Vronsky was not present
reading.correct: Only when she felt too tired and asked for rest
reading.explain: She danced the whole ball except when she felt too tired and asked to rest.

reading.ru: Она знала это чувство и знала его признаки и видела их на Анне, видела дрожащий вспыхивающий блеск в глазах и улыбку счастья и возбуждения, невольно изгибающую губы, и отчетливую грацию, верность и легкость движений.
reading.question: What signs of excitement did Kitty recognize on Anna's face and in her movements?
options: A trembling flashing brightness in her eyes and an involuntary smile of happiness and excitement
A forced, artificial stiffness in her posture
reading.correct: A trembling flashing brightness in her eyes and an involuntary smile of happiness and excitement
reading.explain: Kitty recognized this feeling and its signs on Anna: a trembling, flashing brightness in her eyes and a smile of happiness and excitement involuntarily curving her lips.

reading.ru: Китти посмотрела на него и ужаснулась.
reading.question: How did Kitty react upon looking at Vronsky's face?
reading.explain: Kitty looked at him and was horrified by what she saw on his face.

reading.ru: На лице его было такое выражение, которого она никогда не видала прежде.
reading.question: What was unusual about the expression on Vronsky's face?
options: Kitty had never seen such an expression on him before
It was his usual calm, confident look
It showed anger directed at Kitty
reading.correct: Kitty had never seen such an expression on him before
reading.explain: His face bore an expression she had never seen on him before.

reading.ru: Только пройденная ею строгая школа воспитания поддерживала ее и заставляла делать то, чего от нее требовали, то есть танцевать, отвечать на вопросы, говорить, даже улыбаться.
reading.question: What kept Kitty functioning through her distress at the ball?
options: Her strict upbringing, which forced her to dance, answer, talk, and even smile
A glass of wine she drank quickly
Her mother's constant instructions beside her
The music, which distracted her completely
reading.correct: Her strict upbringing, which forced her to dance, answer, talk, and even smile
reading.explain: Only the strict schooling of her upbringing supported her and made her do what was required — dance, answer questions, talk, even smile.

reading.ru: Она зашла вглубь маленькой гостиной и опустилась на кресло.
reading.question: Where did Kitty go to escape briefly during her despair?
options: Into the depths of a small drawing room, sinking into an armchair
Out onto the balcony for air
To the dance floor to keep dancing
reading.correct: Into the depths of a small drawing room, sinking into an armchair
reading.explain: She went into the depths of a small drawing room and sank into an armchair.

reading.ru: И она опять вспоминала все, что она видела.
reading.question: What did Kitty keep doing while sitting in the armchair?
options: Recalling everything she had seen between Anna and Vronsky
reading.correct: Recalling everything she had seen between Anna and Vronsky
reading.explain: She kept remembering again everything she had seen, doubting whether she was mistaken.

reading.question: How does Kitty respond when Countess Nordston mentions Vronsky asking someone else to dance the mazurka?
options: 'Oh, it's all the same to me'
reading.correct: 'Oh, it's all the same to me'
reading.explain: Kitty answers, 'Oh, it's all the same to me,' trying to hide her distress.

reading.ru: Вронский с Анной сидели почти против нее.
reading.question: Where were Vronsky and Anna seated during the mazurka, relative to Kitty?
options: Behind a pillar, out of sight
reading.explain: Vronsky and Anna sat almost directly across from Kitty during the mazurka.

reading.ru: Она задумывалась, и он становился серьезен.
reading.question: How did Vronsky's mood mirror Anna's during the mazurka?
options: When she grew thoughtful, he became serious
He remained cheerful no matter her mood
He grew angry when she smiled
reading.correct: When she grew thoughtful, he became serious
reading.explain: The text says when Anna grew thoughtful, he became serious too, showing their emotional connection mirrored each other.

reading.ru: Прелестно твердая шея с ниткой жемчуга.
reading.question: What did Kitty find lovely about Anna's neck?
options: Her firm neck with a string of pearls
A scar hidden by a ribbon
reading.correct: Her firm neck with a string of pearls
reading.explain: Kitty thought Anna's firm neck with its string of pearls was lovely, among other admired details.

reading.ru: Китти любовалась ею еще более, чем прежде, и все больше и больше страдала.
reading.question: What contradictory feelings did Kitty experience while watching Anna?
options: She admired her more than ever while suffering more and more
She felt only anger and no admiration
She felt indifferent to Anna's presence
She felt relief that Anna would leave soon
reading.correct: She admired her more than ever while suffering more and more
reading.explain: Kitty admired Anna even more than before, while suffering more and more at the same time.

reading.ru: Китти испуганно смотрела на нее, подходя.
reading.question: How did Kitty look at Anna as she approached her during the mazurka figure?
reading.explain: Kitty looked at Anna with fright as she approached her.

reading.ru: «Полно, Анна Аркадьевна!» — заговорил Корсунский, забирая ее обнаженную руку под рукав своего фрака.
reading.question: How did Korsunsky try to persuade Anna to stay for supper?
options: He took her bare arm under his sleeve while pleading with her
He asked the host to order her to stay
He threatened to stop the music
He asked Vronsky to convince her
reading.correct: He took her bare arm under his sleeve while pleading with her
reading.explain: Korsunsky said 'Come now, Anna Arkadyevna!' while taking her bare arm under the sleeve of his tailcoat, trying to persuade her to stay.

reading.ru: «Нет, я и так в Москве танцевала больше на вашем одном бале, чем всю зиму в Петербурге», — сказала Анна, оглядываясь на подлиннее стоявшего Вронского.
reading.question: What does Anna say about how much she has danced tonight compared to her whole winter in Petersburg?
options: She danced more at this one ball than all winter in Petersburg
She never dances as much in Moscow as in Petersburg
She has not danced at all tonight
She plans to stay all winter in Moscow to dance more
reading.correct: She danced more at this one ball than all winter in Petersburg
reading.explain: Anna says she has already danced more at this single Moscow ball than during the whole winter in Petersburg, glancing at Vronsky as she says it.
